title: Finding Cosine and Tangent from Sine in Quadrant II
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Given that \sin x = 3/5 and x \in [\pi/2, \pi], determine the exact values of \cos x and \tan x.

steps.title: Apply the Pythagorean Identity to Find the Magnitude of Cosine
steps.explanation: Substitute sin x = 3/5 into the Pythagorean identity sin^2 x + cos^2 x = 1 and solve for cos^2 x.
steps.why: The identity sin^2 x + cos^2 x = 1 holds for all real angles x.

steps.title: Select the Correct Sign of Cosine Using the Quadrant of x
steps.explanation: Because x lies in Quadrant II ([pi/2, pi]), the x-coordinate on the unit circle is non-positive, so cos x = -4/5.
steps.why: Cosine is negative in the second quadrant.

steps.title: Calculate the Tangent Ratio
steps.explanation: Divide sin x = 3/5 by cos x = -4/5 to obtain tan x = -3/4.
steps.why: By the quotient identity, tan x = sin x / cos x.
